newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - May 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard was yesterday seized on by the Opposition parties after saying he would not personally be using the savings rebate scheme announced in Tuesday's budget. The scheme has been criticised by the Democrats and Labor as being unfair and they say it should be means-tested. Page 1.

The National Tertiary Education Union has secured pay rises of between 11 and 12.5 percent over the next two years in enterprise agreements with 13 universities. The union will move to finalise similar deals in the higher education sector over the next few months. Page 3.

As Federal Communications Minister Richard Alston looks to be focusing on an option to allow television proprietors to own one newspaper in the same city, government backbenchers fear the issue of media ownership will be pushed through Cabinet. The backbench communications committee will go directly to Prime Minister John Howard to appeal for cabinet to defer its decision on the issue. Page 3.

Democrat Senator Andrew Murray indicated yesterday the Howard government may face its first real threat of a double dissolution over its plans to partially exempt small businesses from unfair dismissal laws. As debate on the issue is schedules for May 26, Murray gave notice in the Senate of a motion to "disallow" the regulations. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday there would be no more spending cuts in the 1998 budget and indicated the A$450 tax rebate on savings could be increased in the lead-up to the next election. Howard also suggested the budget may lead to a lowering of interest rates, saying the Reserve Bank would take budget measures into account when it next meets. Page 1.

Euthanasia doctor Phillip Nitschke announced yesterday at the South Australian Press Club that he is developing a "coma machine" which would allow terminally ill patients to bring on a coma that remained until their death through the administration of drugs. Page 1.

The centrepiece of the Federal Budget should be viewed as a tax handout rather than a tax incentive, as calculations from the budget show there will be no savings made from the Federal Government's new 15 percent tax rebate. The calculations, which assume every person eligible will claim the savings, will mainly reward existing savers. Page 1.

Detective-Sergeant Peter Gallagher revealed yesterday the safety of his three children had been threatened after he detailed corruption to investigators from the New South Wales Police Royal Commission two months ago. Gallagher outlined problems in the elite Internal Affairs unit and the Office of Professional Responsibility, and said the officers who sent him the anonymous threat were still serving. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Federal Government's sales pitch for its budget has been marred after Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday he would not apply for the "universal" savings rebate at the centre of the Budget. Howard's revelation reflected the government's defensiveness over the plan, which allows people putting money into superannuation and bank accounts to claim a 15 percent tax rebate. Page 1.

In a response to the budget that could embarrass the government, leading savings expert Vince Fitzgerald said yesterday that the new rebate may have a negative impact on national savings, for while it should encourage more private savings, it would be unlikely this would offset the costs of the A$2 billion scheme. Page 1.

The Monteagle Public School in Young has banned the traditional Easter play based on the trial and death of Christ, saying it is too violent for children and against New South Wales Government guidelines. Principal Julie Newbury said yesterday the decision was supported by the State Government and the Department of School Education. Page 1.

The New South Wales Department of School Education has bowed to pressure from gay groups and will introduce a controversial new programme designed to stop gay vilification in state schools from July. The trial programme will be tested in six primary and two econdary schools in Sydney. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Auditor-General Ches Baragwanath yesterday urged Coalition MPs to go against the party line and vote for the protection of his office. Baragwanath's direct plea to Parliament came as he warned proposed government changes to his office may render Parliament impotent to fight oppression and corruption by any future government. Page 1.

Victorian Auditor-General Ches Baragwanath says schools in the state are becomingly more and more reliant on local communities for funding, as figures reveal 97 percent of schools have had to introduce voluntary levies. About 16 percent of non-salary csts for schools across the state was contributed by parents. Page 1.

Federal Primary Industries Minister John Anderson moved to reassure the public yesterday as quarantine authorities work to protect fruit-growing regions from fire blight, a potentially devastating plant disease discovered in Melbourne's Botanic Gardens. Page 1.

Police believe they have found the body of the man suspected of killing three people near Swan Hill on Sunday. Chief Superintendent David Mansell said the body of the man was found by police dogs in dense bush, with a firearm by its side, and several other firearms in a nearby truck. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
